$comment: Starling mode-routing contract: one typed, versioned mode entry (E18).
A mode is DATA. It names intent, behavior, the leading-phrase routing
flags, scoped vocabulary/snippets, the selection role, delivery policy
and processing-route descriptors. It cannot encode permission elevation:
privacy/transmission grants belong to runtime and user policy and are
frozen at activation (MODES_AND_CONTEXT.md); no mode field adds
providers, grants or network endpoints.
Alias gating (E26): aliases are leading spoken phrases matched only at
the start of a take after permitted whitespace, on whole-token
boundaries, with a finite separator set (space or colon). They fire only
when the session allows aliases, the take is not a locked manual choice,
and the resolved profile sets allow_spoken_overrides true. Verbatim
modes set allow_spoken_overrides false by default, so dictated words
stay literal in them. Longest unambiguous alias wins (token count, then
character length); an alias shared across modes at equal best rank is a
conflict needing resolution, never a guess. A leading 'literal' escape
selects verbatim payload handling ahead of any alias.
This file validates a single mode entry. profiles.schema.json embeds the
identical entry schema as its profiles items and adds the surrounding
resolution document (default profile plus scoped rules);
tests/test_mode_routing.py asserts the two cannot drift.
Keyword subset: only keywords the repo's minischema.py fallback
understands are used, so jsonschema and minischema agree. Cross-field
rules a JSON Schema cannot express (unique ids, valid default, verbatim
profile present, local-only vs remote route, replace_selection requires
edit-target authority, alias uniqueness) are enforced by the executable
oracle tests/mode_routing.py validate_config.

version.description: Version of this mode definition; decisions record it as mode_version.

aliases.description: Enabled leading spoken phrases (code this, edit this). Leading-position, whole-token matches only.

allow_spoken_overrides.description: Verbatim flag: false disables this mode's aliases and keeps leading phrases literal. Verbatim modes ship false by default.

vocabulary.description: Scoped recognition-bias terms for this mode; never a provider or permission.

snippets.description: Scoped spoken-to-text expansions applied in this mode only.
